title: Legible Cities engine protocol, version 1
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout with Content-Length framing. `methods` maps each request to the schema of its params and result; `notifications` maps each notification to the schema of its params. Long requests (graph.build, map.build, export.encode, feeds.service, feeds.inspect, feeds.add, feeds.remove, render.stage) stay open until done and send job/progress and job/log carrying the request's id meanwhile; $/cancelRequest ends the process they are waiting on (a LOOM tool, or ffmpeg) and they answer with the cancelled error (-32800). feeds.service starts no process: a cancel is answered with the same error once its read finishes. feeds.remove has a point of no return, the write of the registry: a cancel before it leaves the feed registered with every file in place and is answered with the same error, and one after it is not honoured (the feed is already forgotten and its files are removed to the end) and is said so in the answer. A feed a long request downloads stops at the cancel, between chunks or once it has arrived, and nothing of it is cached; on a server that has stopped sending, the cancel waits for the next chunk or the read timeout. The export methods are the two halves of an export a client cannot do itself: export.plan describes one and is pure, export.encode turns the frames the client captured into the file; there is no export.capture, because the desktop app captures for itself. Errors a person can act on are code -32000 with `data` of the ErrorData shape; bad parameters are -32602 with the same shape and kind `params`.

RequestId.description: A JSON-RPC request id, as the client chose it.

NoParams.description: The method takes no parameters: omit `params`, or send an empty object.

FeedKey.description: The key of a registered feed: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, as in the engine's registry and its file names.

Token.description: A folder name under the engine's home, never a path: the desktop app passes its project id.

FeedsServiceParams.description: Ask when a feed runs and which day to draw: its service window and the busiest weekday scanning from an anchor. A long request, like graph.build: it downloads the feed when it is not cached, reporting that download's bytes as job/progress (stage download), and reads its calendar and trips, which sends no progress.

anchor.description: The day to scan from; the engine's today when omitted, and echoed either way so a caller can store it. An anchor outside the window scans from the window's middle.

lines.description: The lines the map draws, as graph.build names them in stages.octi.lines. Trips are counted on those lines, as the map build counts them, so the day is the map's; every trip in the feed counts when omitted.

start.description: The first day the feed's calendar covers.

busiest_weekday.description: The weekday in the window with the most trips, scanning from the anchor: the same feed and anchor give the same day on every machine.

anchor.description: The anchor the choice was made from.

ServiceDate.description: A calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. map.build never picks one, because its choice would depend on the day the request was made; feeds.service picks one from an anchor the caller gives.

EngineInfo.description: The handshake. A client refuses to continue unless `protocol` is the version it was built for and `engine` is the tag it pinned.

engine.description: The engine's version, as in its package metadata.

commit.description: The LOOM commit the binaries were built from; null when the backend cannot say.

ffmpeg.description: The ffmpeg the engine would run (SCHEMATIC_FFMPEG, else the first on PATH), or null.

home.description: SCHEMATIC_HOME as resolved: where feeds, graphs and output live.

LayoutId.description: A stored layout's id: the sha256, as 64 hex digits, of everything that went into it. The same feed, options and LOOM name the same id before anything runs; the desktop app stores it with a project.

HexColor.description: A colour a client chooses, written #rrggbb. The feed's own route_color arrives without the hash and is the feed's, not the client's.

LayoutMeta.description: What a stored layout was made from, as written beside it in .meta.json. The inputs are what its id hashes; engine, made and migrated are not.

feed_sha256.description: The sha256 of the feed zip as downloaded.

loom.description: The LOOM commit the host passed as SCHEMATIC_LOOM_COMMIT; null when it was not told.

stages.description: The graph-to-graph stages and their arguments, in order.

engine.description: The engine version that made it.

made.description: When, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

migrated.description: True for a set from before layouts had names, moved under its id once; its inputs are the feed and options as they were at migration.

GraphBuildParams.description: Lay a registered feed out: gtfs2graph, topo, loom and octi, stored under the home as one layout named by the hash of its inputs (the feed's bytes, the mode, the agency, the label options, the LOOM build). The same inputs name the same layout; a layout already stored is answered without running anything. Mode, agency and the label options default to the registry entry.

mode.description: What gtfs2graph keeps of the feed (LOOM's -m): names such as tram, subway, rail, bus, ferry or all, or route_type numbers, comma-joined for several; the registry entry's when omitted.

agency.description: Keep only this agency_id; the registry entry's when omitted; empty for every operator, whatever the entry says.

label_pattern.description: A regular expression applied to route_long_name when route_short_name is blank; group 1 is the line's label.

label_strip.description: A regular expression removed from every label.

force.description: Lay the feed out again under the same id. The stored layout stays until the new set is whole, then is replaced; a new layout may place stations differently.

octilinear.description: The share of drawn length on a 45-degree multiple; only the octi stage carries it.

paths.description: Where each stage's GeoJSON is stored, as absolute paths under the home: graphs/<key>/<layout>/.

MapBuildParams.description: Draw the map, the animation page and a thumbnail pair for a registered feed on one service day, from a stored layout. Never lays the feed out: a layout that is not stored is refused, with a hint to lay it out first.

out.description: The folder under the home's out/ to write into. Omitted, the files go into out/ itself.

width.description: The SVG's width in CSS pixels.

colors.description: A colour per line label, over the feed's own route_color. A label the layout does not carry is ignored, so a client can keep colours for lines a narrower mode dropped.

default_color.description: The colour of a line the feed leaves uncoloured, on the map and in the page's chips, dots and chart alike; #888888 when omitted.

line_order.description: Line labels in the order they stack on shared track, the later over the earlier, and the order of the page's rows in the Linear and Time views. A line the list leaves out follows the ones it names, and a label the layout does not carry is ignored, so a partial or stale order never drops a line.

lines.description: A display name and a hidden flag per line, keyed by line label. A label the layout does not carry is ignored, so a client can keep its choices for lines a narrower mode dropped. Hiding is a drawing choice: a hidden line comes off the map, its trips, the page and the thumbnails, a station only it served is not drawn, and no stored layout changes; render.stage still shows every line.

MapStyle.description: How the map is drawn, in the engine's own numbers. Every field is optional; omitting the object, or any field, draws exactly what is drawn without it. The numbers are in SVG user units at the map's width (the map is fitted to MapBuildParams.width, 1800 by default, so a line width of 7 is seven of 1800), except line_gap, a multiple of line_width. interchange_radius may not be below station_radius, judged on the values the map would be drawn with (a field left out counts as its default): a rule the schema cannot hold and the server does. label_size and label_offset re-place the labels and move the drawing's viewBox, never the stored layout. The four colours are the literals a standalone SVG falls back to; the animation page's theme overrides them, which is why the desktop app does not send them.

line_width.description: Line stroke width, in SVG user units at the map's width; 7 when omitted.

line_gap.description: Pitch of parallel tracks as a multiple of line_width, so it has no unit; 1.6 when omitted.

station_radius.description: Radius of a station on one route, in SVG user units at the map's width; 4.2 when omitted.

interchange_radius.description: Radius of a station where routes meet, in SVG user units at the map's width; 6 when omitted. Not below station_radius.

station_stroke.description: Width of a station's outline, in SVG user units at the map's width; 2.2 when omitted.

label_size.description: Font size of a station's name, in SVG user units at the map's width; 11 when omitted. The labels are placed again, so the viewBox moves.

label_offset.description: Distance of a name from its station, in SVG user units at the map's width; 9 when omitted. The labels are placed again, so the viewBox moves.

padding.description: Margin round the drawing on every side, in SVG user units at the map's width; 24 when omitted.

background.description: The ground, as the literal a standalone SVG falls back to; the page's theme overrides it. #ffffff when omitted.

station_fill.description: A station's fill, as the literal a standalone SVG falls back to; the page's theme overrides it. #ffffff when omitted.

station_stroke_color.description: A station's outline, as the literal a standalone SVG falls back to; the page's theme overrides it. #111111 when omitted.

label_color.description: The station names, as the literal a standalone SVG falls back to; the page's theme overrides it. #111111 when omitted.

LineOptions.description: What a client chose for one line of the map. Every field is optional; an empty object changes nothing.

name.description: The line's display name, written where the page writes the line's label: its chip, its row and the time chart's band, and the trains' titles. The label stays the line's key everywhere else (the SVG's data-line, ExportOptions.lines). From 1 to 40 characters, with no line break.

hidden.description: True leaves the line off the map: no track, no trips, no chip, row or band, and no colour in the thumbnails; the lines it shared track with close up over its place.

unmatched.description: The first few stop ids that matched no node.

thumb_dark.description: A small picture of the map for the dark palette: the network alone, about 400 units wide, no ground, every colour a literal, in the request's colors, default_color and line_order. Safe to show in an img.

thumb_light.description: The same picture for the light palette.

stations.description: Every station the map draws, sorted by name as code points and then by id: what a client offers to pick a trip from. A station only a hidden line served is not drawn and not listed.

id.description: The station's node id in the stored layout: what the page's window.__present.setTrip takes.

name.description: The name the map writes for it; the empty string where the feed gives none.

summary.description: Result.summary(), the lines the CLI prints.

caveats.description: What the build had to fudge, as sentences a person can read: the atlas's caveats, from the same numbers.

issues.description: How much of the network the build had to fudge, as one weighted proportion; 0 is clean. What the atlas is ordered by.

JobProgress.description: Sent while a long request runs, once per step as it finishes. A feed downloaded inside any long request -- a preset's zip fetched the first time a layout, an inspection, a service-day read or a draw needs it -- reports stage download when that download happens, once per chunk: its fraction is of the download's own bytes (0 when the server did not say how many), not of the request, and its message counts them; the request's own steps follow with their fractions of the request. A feed already on disk reports no download.

JobLog.description: A line a tool wrote to stderr while a long request ran, as it arrived.

PresetName.description: A preset's name; export.presets describes each. Held equal to the engine's table by a test.

StoryboardName.description: A storyboard's name; export.storyboards describes each. Held equal to the engine's table by a test.

View.description: A view the page can show.

Clock.description: A time of day, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS; past midnight stays past midnight (25:44 is 1:44 the next morning).

Caption.description: A person's words for the frame, 1 to 80 characters with no line break. The page draws it as text, never markup, under the title at the size of the date line: at most two lines at 1,080 wide.

ClockCorner.description: Where the page draws the clock. Left out, it is bottom-right, where the clock has always sat, except on a preset with safe zones (instagram-reel, instagram-story), where it is top-right: there bottom-right is refused, because the platform's own interface covers it, and bottom-left comes with a note.

PageUrl.description: The page's own address, with its scheme. The desktop app serves a project's page on its own origin and passes that; the engine's default is the site's file.

AbsolutePath.description: A path the client owns, absolute, never inside the engine's own repository.

Preset.description: One destination, with the dimensions and limits that destination has.

storyboard.description: Video only: the storyboard the preset plays unless told otherwise.

max_bytes.description: The platform's upload limit, where it has one.

safe_zones.description: Whether the platform draws its own interface over the image.

StoryboardBeat.description: A stretch of video with one set of state, as the storyboard is written; export.storyboards answers every field, and a client writing a list gives only secs and what changes. A field left out or null carries over from the beat before. The server also checks what this cannot say: the beats last 90 seconds in all at most, a span's first clock is before its second, the first beat names a view and has tween 0 or none, since frame 0 must already be in a view, and the first beat names at unless it sweeps without hours, since frame 0 is not reproducible without a clock.

views.description: The views it visits, in order, as a sentence fragment; empty for one view.

geographic.description: Whether any beat needs the feed's geographic geometry.

ExportOptions.description: The dressing of an export; every field optional and defaulted as bin/export defaults it.

view.description: The view a still is taken in. For a video it opens a named storyboard: the first beat takes it, with no transition. Refused beside a list on a video preset, whose first beat names its view.

title.description: The city and network over the map.

at.description: The clock to start at; a still is taken here. For a video it opens a named storyboard, as its first beat's clock. Refused beside a list on a video preset, whose first beat carries its own.

lines.description: Line labels to keep; the rest are hidden.

storyboard.description: What a video plays: a storyboard's name, or a list of beats written as export.storyboards writes them, played in order. A list's first beat names the view frame 0 is in, and its clock unless it sweeps without hours. A still ignores either.

quality.description: draft: 1x and fast; standard: 2x, resampled to the preset's size; high: 2x, kept.

tag.description: A filename suffix, so two dressings of one preset can share a folder.

safe.description: Draw the platform's safe zones; never for a deliverable.

ExportPlanParams.description: Describe an export: what to capture and how to encode it. Pure and instant; nothing is written. A vector preset is refused (it is resolved from the built map, not captured).

date.description: The service day the title names, when the caller knows it (the app's project does).

BeatPayload.description: A beat as the recorder takes it: times in seconds of the service day, the span resolved.

CaptureJob.description: One export, described: the capture half is the job the engine's own recorder takes (url, width, height in CSS pixels, scale, fps, format, settle, beats, at); the rest is what export.encode needs afterwards. Handed back to export.encode unchanged.

settle.description: Milliseconds to wait, with the clock stopped, for the page's first geometry pass and its fonts.

keep.description: Deliver the captured pixels as they are rather than resampling to the preset's size.

storyboard.description: The storyboard's name; custom for a list of beats; empty for a still.

at.description: The clock, in seconds, a still is taken at; a video's beats seek for themselves.

notes.description: What a person should hear before the capture, such as a sweep too fast to read.

caption.description: The caption as given; null for none.

clock_corner.description: The corner resolved, given even where the clock is off and the address names none.

filename.description: stem plus the format's extension; the plan's convenience.

Provenance.description: What the caller knows about the map that the atlas's data would not; it goes into the sidecar over the atlas's, field by field.

alt.description: The sidecar's alt text in the caller's own words, written trimmed, in place of the description the engine generates; omitted, the generated one stands. At most 1,000 characters, counted as Unicode code points (a JavaScript string's length counts UTF-16 units, so one emoji is one here and two there). Text of only whitespace is refused by the server.

ExportEncodeParams.description: The frames the client captured (a directory of 000000.png onwards), or its still, to the deliverable at dest with its sidecar beside it. The source is read and never touched; a cancel, a failure or a file over the platform's limit leaves nothing at dest.

source.description: The frames directory for a video plan, the captured still for a still plan.

dest.description: The file to write; its folder is created.

sidecar.description: The sidecar as written beside the file: what it is, the network's caveats, alt text.

FeedRecord.description: A registry entry, preset or added by a person: what the engine knows about a feed before it reads it. `cached` says whether its zip is on disk.

url.description: Where the zip came from; empty for a feed added from a file.

headways.description: Whether the feed's service is run from frequencies.txt (trains at a scheduled interval) rather than a timetable of trip times. A preset says so in the registry; for a feed added through feeds.add it is decided when the zip is checked: frequencies.txt has rows and the trips they name in trips.txt are at least half of the feed's trips.

source.description: Which half of the registry: a preset is curated in the engine and cannot be removed; a user feed was added through feeds.add.

FeedsAddParams.description: Add a feed a person chose, from a URL or a zip the client owns, and keep it across restarts. A long request: the download reports its bytes as job/progress (stage download), then the check reports once (stage check). The zip must carry stops, routes, trips, stop_times and a calendar in one of its two forms; a refusal names the missing table and leaves nothing behind. A cancel is honoured until the moment the feed is kept, and answers with the cancelled error (-32800): the feed is then in neither the registry nor the cache, so a client told an add was cancelled need not go looking for one. The name defaults to the feed's first agency, the key to a slug of the name made unique.

source.description: A URL with its scheme, or an absolute path to a zip the client owns.

mode.description: What gtfs2graph keeps of the feed (LOOM's -m); all when omitted. feeds.inspect suggests one.

agency.description: Keep only this agency_id; every operator when omitted.

FeedsRemoveParams.description: Forget a feed a person added, with its zips and its stored layouts. A preset is refused with kind feed. A long request: the registry's write is the point of no return, and a cancel before it leaves the feed registered with every file in place.

FeedsRemoveResult.description: The feed is forgotten and its files are gone. `cancel_too_late` is present, and true, only when a cancel arrived after the point of no return and so was not honoured; otherwise the answer is exactly `{"ok": true}`.

FeedsInspectParams.description: What is in a feed, as data, before anything is laid out: read from the raw zip, never the agency-filtered copy, so the answer is what a choice of mode and agency is made from. A long request when the feed is not cached; a few seconds for a large one. Never reads stop_times.

anchor.description: The day the service choice scans from, as feeds.service takes it; the engine's today when omitted, and echoed.

label.description: The label the map would draw: route_short_name, or the long name through the feed's label pattern, then the strip.

route_type.description: GTFS route_type as published; -1 when missing.

color.description: route_color as the spec asks for it: six hex digits, upper case, without the hash. Null when the feed leaves it out or writes something that is not a colour, which a client must not paint with.

text_color.description: route_text_color on the same terms as color.

trips.description: Rows in trips.txt; a headway-based trip is a template that expands into runs.

name.description: The GTFS name: tram, subway, rail, bus, ferry, cable tram, aerial lift, funicular, trolleybus, monorail; an extended code says which it folds onto.

mode.description: The LOOM mode (gtfs2graph -m) that keeps this type, so a client can show which types a chosen mode draws; null for a type LOOM has no name for. The mode all keeps every type.

modes.description: Every -m name that keeps this type, the canonical one first (subway and metro; tram and streetcar; rail and train); empty for a type LOOM has no name for. A numeric mode keeps its own code.

StopCounts.description: Rows of stops.txt by location_type, and the total.

Inspection.description: A feed as the Inspect screen shows it.

tables.description: The GTFS tables present, by stem.

frequency_trips.description: Trips with frequencies.txt windows: templates, expanded into runs when the day is built.

service.description: The window and the engine's day from the anchor, as feeds.service answers them; null when the feed has no calendar, with a warning saying so.

suggested_mode.description: A LOOM mode from the route types: all for a feed with nothing but rail-like types, else the most common rail-like type, else the most common. The app shows it; the person decides.

warnings.description: Sentences for a person: a headway-based timetable, an expired or unstarted calendar, a calendar_dates-only schedule, routes without short names, several operators in one feed.

StageName.description: One of the pipeline's four stages, in order.

RenderStageParams.description: One stored stage graph of a layout, drawn as SVG, with its counts (E15) and its description (StageDescription): what a geographic view shows beside the schematic map, and what its text alternative is written from. Never lays out; a stage that is not stored is refused with kind layout.

width.description: The drawing's width in CSS pixels; the canvas grows for labels.

date.description: The project's service day, which times each line of the description by its commonest trip that day. Left out, every trip and the extent are null and no timetable is read: the engine never picks a day for it. Null is refused; leave it out instead.

svg.description: A self-contained SVG document, themed through CSS variables with literal fallbacks.

StageDescription.description: The stage graph drawn, in fields a text alternative is written from; the engine writes no sentence. A station is named as the map draws it, the empty string where the feed gives no name, never its id; a junction LOOM inserted (no station) is never named, listed or met at. The minutes are of the layout and the request's date, not of the stage, so every stage answers the same ones; only the order of their two names follows the stage.

extent.description: The line whose trip takes the most minutes, with that trip; the first in label order on a tie. Null without a date, or when no line has a trip that day.

lines.description: One entry per line label, in label order (sorted). For every line, its stations and every branch's together are the line's stations, each once.

termini.description: The first and last station of the line's spine, its longest run (linear.spine), never a headsign; one for a loop, or for a spine of one station.

stations.description: The spine's stations in order, termini first and last. A loop, a line whose graph is one cycle, lists its cycle once, from the station with the smallest node id toward that station's neighbour with the smaller id.

meets.description: Every station of the line whose node carries another line on any edge, in the order of stations and then of each branch's stations.

lines.description: The other lines there, in label order.

branches.description: The stations off the spine, as simple paths in travel order: from each spine station in order, each way off it in node id order, a branch and then the branches that fork from it. A branch ends where it forks again, and each way on from the fork is a branch of its own. Empty for a loop.

at.description: The station the branch leaves. Where it leaves the run at a junction that is not a station, the station next to the junction along that run on the side with more stations to the run's end, toward its start on a tie; where it leaves a junction ending a branch, the nearest station back along that branch, else that branch's own at. Null for a further piece of the line that touches the rest nowhere, whose stations are that piece's own spine and whose branches follow it.

stations.description: In travel order away from at. A branch that would pass no station is left out; the branches beyond it are kept.

trip.description: The line's commonest trip on the date: its trips that day grouped by their first and last calls at a mapped station, the largest group winning (on a tie the shorter median, then the names that sort first), its median duration in whole minutes rounded half up. from and to are in the order the line's stations and then its branches list them, a name the stage does not list keeping the trip's own order; equal for a trip that ends where it began. Null without a date, or when the line has no trip that day.

ErrorData.description: The `data` of an error response. `hint` is a sentence for a person and is what a UI shows; `detail` says where, for a log.
